source_documents.title: Aggregation-Modulated Excited-State Intramolecular Proton Transfer and Antifungal Potential of Selected 1,3,4-Thiadiazole Derivatives

reference_evidence_units.quote: The spectroscopic results support the occurrence of excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) in both derivatives and indicate that this process is facilitated by molecular aggregation.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PhTD-ClB and FTD-EtB
reference_evidence_units.statement: ESIPT (enol/keto emission) in both compounds, favoured by aggregation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Steady-state and TCSPC data; no excited-state calculation of the proton transfer.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The combined fluorescence and RLS results indicate that molecular aggregation modifies the balance between the enol- and keto-related emission pathways and promotes an AIE-like enhancement of the ESIPT-associated long-wavelength emission.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PhTD-ClB and FTD-EtB
reference_evidence_units.statement: Aggregation shifts the enol/keto emission balance and enhances keto emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The intermolecular interaction behind the enhancement is not identified.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Assuming a card-pack arrangement, Kasha’s exciton model yields approximate intermolecular separations of 3.65 Å for PhTD-ClB and 3.77 Å for FTD-EtB.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PhTD-ClB and FTD-EtB
reference_evidence_units.statement: Exciton-splitting analysis of hypsochromic absorption components (card-pack, H-type geometry).

reference_mechanisms.label: ESIPT_PT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: ESIPT (dual enol/keto fluorescence) is the paper's main explanation; supported by steady-state and lifetime data only.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Aggregation (H-type card-pack exciton coupling from absorption) modulates the ESIPT emission balance.
